terms.meaning: making names defined in one file available from another file.
the list of names a package declares as its public interface.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Package front door
sections.what: Brings the contract models and service functions into one place and declares which names are public. Other code can then import them from the package.
sections.why: Likely reason: it keeps imports short and hides the internal file layout.
sections.watch_out: Keep the export list in step with the imports, or a name will be missing for callers.

summary: Re-exports the public names from the integrations contract and service modules so other code can import them from one place.
purpose: Acts as the front door of the integrations package.
why: Likely reason: callers import from one package name and do not need to know the internal file layout.
how: Imports four contract models and four service functions, then lists the same eight names in an export list.
inputs: None. This file only loads other modules.
outputs: The eight names become available to importers of the package.
risks: A name added to the imports but not to the export list is not exposed by the package. Importing the package also loads the service module.
debug: If an import of one of these names fails, check that the name appears in both the import block and the export list, and that the source module defines it.
